newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SMITH PLAYS DOWN RANGERS' BIG LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SMITH PLAYS DOWN RANGERS' BIG LEAD.

text.p: Most soccer managers would be ecstatic to find their team 12 points clear of the field half way through the league season but Glasgow Rangers' Walter Smith says it is no big deal.
"We have made a reasonable start, no better than that," said Smith, whose side enter Saturday's premier division match at Hearts on the back of their 4-2 win over Kilmarnock on Tuesday.
"We have lost a few points in games where we were in a winning position, but needless to say every team could probably say that looking back at this stage.
"Given the sheer number of games we have had so far -- Tuesday was our 30th competitive match -- I have to be relatively pleased that we are out in front."

And although Rangers are 14 points ahead of arch-rivals Celtic, whose record of nine consecutive Scottish league titles they are attempting to equal this season, for Smith the gap between the two Glasgow giants is only five points.
Celtic have three matches in hand on the defending champions and Smith, ever the cautious manager, is banking on them winning all three.
As for Hearts, a massive 20 points off the pace, Saturday's match represents the first opportunity to exact revenge for their 4-3 defeat by Rangers in last month's League Cup final.
"Hearts will be desperate to atone for that defeat and they are always capable of troubling any opposition, particularly at Tynecastle," Smith said.
And Hearts manager Jim Jefferies added: "We showed in the final we could match Rangers and this game gives us a chance to make up for recent disappointments."

Smith has the Scottish league's record goalscorer Ally McCoist back to full fitness but might leave him on the bench in favour of Dane Erik Bo Anderson, who scored a hat-trick in McCoist's absence on Tuesday.
Rangers' midweek win also marked the return of defender Alan McLaren from a seven-month injury absence, although he is still struggling for match-fitness.
"Alan came through his comeback with no ill effects but we won't use him in every game over the holiday period," Smith said.

Hearts, who have Italian defender Pasquale Bruno suspended and a further five players injured, enter the clash after two consecutive defeats, the first at home to Aberdeen, the second at bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock.
The Edinburgh side have never lost three consecutive league games under Jefferies, and they will know Rangers will test that record to breaking point.
